source.title: Behavior Beyond Text: Evaluating Refusal Transfer Failure in LLM Agents
source.authors: Ekagra Gupta; R. Saha; Aniekan-Abasi Inyang; Adam Al Gharib

page_placements.theme: Chat refusal does not guarantee safe agent or tool actions

record.file_problem: None noted; the full paper and appendix are present.
record.tranche_reason: The study reports results about whether text refusals transfer to tool-call actions, a related but different construct from the listed claim versions. It does not test fine-tuning effects, per-token KL concentration, opening-token bypasses, weight or rank localization, causes of shallow safety, or deepening methods.
record.gate_note: The paper evaluates harmful-request refusal and unsafe tool calls in matched text-only and tool-enabled settings, and probes a refusal-associated activation direction. These results concern action selection in tool-enabled agents, not the specific interventions or measurements named by V1–V7. Mentioned claims and results from cited studies are not recorded as rows.
record.test_reason: The study measures whether text refusals carry over to unsafe tool calls, and probes a refusal activation direction. It has no harmful or benign fine-tuning (V1, V2) and no per-token KL between aligned and base models (V3). It uses no prefill, suffix or decoding change (V4); stress mode is jailbreak-style user framing, not a forced compliant opening. It does not localize safety in weights or ranks (V5), since the direction ablated is an activation direction. It has no causal test of the training data or objective (V6) and no deepening training (V7). Qi et al. 2024 is cited only once, as an interpretation in the Discussion. These findings belong under fits_no_version.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct, with additions. The authors also report that tool context weakens the refusal signal in four of five models. They add that interventions mainly change whether a model calls a tool, not the unsafe rate among calls made, and that tool-call safety must be evaluated directly.
record.recipe_differences: The study evaluates matched text and tool-call prompts and uses activation-direction interventions; it does not reproduce the fine-tuning or token-depth methods in the original sources.
record.method_sensitivity: Transfer divergence varies with tool-prompt mode and system-prompt framing. Stress mode raises divergence for some models; safety-reinforced prompts reduce it but do not close it. Tool-encouraging prompts increase it for Mistral and Command-R. Refusal-direction effects also vary across models.

fits_no_version.finding: Under normal tool prompting, 0.098–0.519 of harmful requests refused in chat yield unsafe tool calls (0.098–0.657 under stress) across five instruct models. Safety-reinforced system prompts reduce but do not close the gap; tool-encouraging prompts widen it for Mistral and Command-R.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Text refusal does not reliably transfer to tool-call safety in tool-enabled agents.

fits_no_version.finding: Refusal-direction activation drops from no-tool to tool prompts in 4/5 models (Llama null, t=0.4). It predicts unsafe calls (AUC 0.76–0.86), but patching reverts 13–90% of unsafe calls, mostly by suppressing the call. Ablation raises refusal in Qwen and Gemma and lowers it in the other three.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: A refusal activation direction partly mediates whether a model acts with tools, but not how safely it acts.

record.problems: The authors state that tool availability is varied jointly with tool-oriented prompt wording, so the remaining failures cannot be attributed specifically to tool affordance. The harness tests generated calls rather than executing them, and is single-step. Refusal-direction admissibility checks fail for some models; the paper also reports degenerate intervention outputs in some conditions.
record.rows_left_out: The 60-row cap was reached. Omitted additional reported outcomes include the direction cosine comparisons and KL-admissibility and random/mean-direction controls in Tables 5–6; activation-addition benign-refusal sweep in Table 7; tool-call ablation outcomes in Table 8; and coefficient-by-coefficient steering results, including benign-call costs and degeneracy, in Table 9. These were lower priority than the model-by-condition behavioral outcomes and the main suppression, patching, prediction, and ablation results.

untested.parts: No per-token KL between aligned and base models.
No prefilling, adversarial suffixes or decoding changes. Tool context and jailbreak-style framing are a different manipulation.
No weight or rank localization. Only an activation-space refusal direction is probed.
No test of data or objective as the cause of shallowness.
No deepening training or its robustness.

record.verdict_notes: The record's relation 'discusses' and tranche T6 are confirmed. The only link to shallow alignment is a Discussion sentence treating suppression of the shared direction as consistent with Qi et al. 2024. That sentence is interpretation, not a test. The steering cost results (Table 9) are omitted per rows_left_out; they would also fall under fits_no_version.

versions.untested_parts: No harmful fine-tuning or fine-tuning data-size intervention.
No per-token KL measurement between aligned and base models.
No compliant-opening prefills, adversarial suffixes, or decoding changes.
No test of whether a small set of weights or ranks carries safety behaviour.
No test of training data or objective as the cause of shallowness.
No training intended to deepen safety and no evaluation of whether such training holds up.

relation.reason: Section 6 relates refusal-signal suppression to Qi et al. (2024), but the study neither tests the specified claim versions nor uses their findings as an experimental tool.

tranche.reason: Measures text-to-tool refusal transfer and activation-direction interventions, without testing V1–V7. A residual-stream direction is not a small subset of weights or ranks. Tool prompting changes neither response prefixes nor decoding. Section 6 discusses shallow alignment as related evidence.

source_check.notes: Table 2 reports system-condition subsets, whereas Table 1 pools system conditions; neutral values are not pooled baselines. The authors' conclusion is accurately represented; tool availability and tool-oriented prompt wording vary jointly, limiting causal attribution.
